rationale:
WHAT IS WRONG. One question -- 'which agent's workflow is this context executing?' -- is answered by two ladders in two packages, and they disagree in production. coordinator.determineOwnerAgentType (coordinator.go:3466) climbs RunAgentType -> Sender.AgentType -> os.Getenv(AGENT_TYPE) -> log Error -> 'generic', and fills orchestration_states.owner_agent_type. actions.runningStepProvenance (actions/log_action_error.go:118) implemented only the SECOND rung, and fills agent_error_log.agent_type/step_name for the RSH-008 provenance door. So a row filed under 'the running step' recorded the dispatch-path sender -- literally 'generic' on the generic dispatch path -- while the orchestration row for the SAME run recorded the real agent. types/context.go:62 documents RunAgentType as 'the RESOLVED real agent type whose workflow is executing ... as opposed to the dispatch-path sender which is often generic', and until this change the coordinator was its ONLY reader.

THE FIX. Hoist the two CONTEXT rungs onto the shared type as (*types.ExecutionContext).ResolvedAgentType(), and have both consumers climb it. One ladder, two consumers, no drift. Reachability was checked with the compiler, not asserted: actions cannot import orchestration (the cycle is real, so delegating coordinator-ward is not an option), and types IS imported by both (go list -f '{{range .Imports}}' on each package: orchestration -> actions found; both -> types = 1).

THE DESIGN DECISION, which is where this could have re-created the drift rather than fixed it. The coordinator's two REMAINING rungs -- os.Getenv(AGENT_TYPE) and the 'generic' filler -- deliberately do NOT move. AGENT_TYPE is a property of the PROCESS, not of the message, and ExecutionContext is deserialised from Kafka headers; a method whose answer changes with the pod it is called on is invisible at the call site and untestable without mutating the environment. More importantly the two consumers legitimately DISAGREE about what follows the context, and that disagreement is correct rather than drift: the coordinator falls back to the pod and then to a filler because owner_agent_type is NOT NULL and a row must be written; the actions door falls back to params.AgentType -- which IS state.OwnerAgentType, this ladder's own durable output, so strictly more specific than the pod -- and must not reach for a filler at all, because an unresolvable provenance there lands as 'unattributed' by RSH-008's design (OWNER RULING 2026-08-02, RFC_010 section 2). A ResolvedAgentType(fallback string) taking the tail as a parameter was the obvious alternative and is worse: two callers passing different fallbacks is the same drift wearing a shared-helper costume. TestResolvedAgentType_IgnoresTheProcessEnvironment pins the exclusion with t.Setenv, so a future author cannot 'complete' the ladder without a red test.

THE SIZING IN THE HANDOFF THAT COMMISSIONED THIS WORK WAS STALE, AND I AM CORRECTING IT RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. It cited generic = 559 rows over 25 distinct step_names, and 25 REVIEW_SUPERSEDED_BY_PASSING_SAVE rows all carrying generic, as live damage. Re-measured at the rows 2026-08-08: 499 of the 555 were written BEFORE 2026-07-26, the day RunAgentType itself shipped (baf887a8e) -- the coordinator's own ladder already removed ~89% of them, and the dominant producer (call_agent/call_dispatch, 394 rows) stops dead on 2026-07-25. All 25 REVIEW_SUPERSEDED rows are from 2026-07-23 and that action has not filed one since. The residue this change actually addresses is ~36 rows in 13 days, from the three actions-door producers. So the case is STRUCTURAL -- one ladder, two consumers -- and is NOT a volume argument. I would rather the seats judged the real number.

CONSUMERS, NAMED RATHER THAN MERELY MEASURED (OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 section 3). No automated consumer branches on the VALUE of agent_error_log.agent_type. Three Go readers: diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:265 renders it into the diagnosis bundle; reconcile_superseded_reviews_action.go:223 filters site_id + error_code + context->>'page_name'; page_build_failure_guard.go:131 filters error_code + context->>'page_id'. Live agent config: 0 steps filter on it -- the only three whose SQL names the table (council-gate, feature-designer, fix-proposer) are load_schema_hint steps reading information_schema.columns. Repo SQL: sql_for_agents/214_build_dispatch_watchdog.sql:109 selects it for display. So the consumers are HUMANS and the diagnosis bundle, through idx_error_log_agent (agent_type, occurred_at DESC). orchestration_states.owner_agent_type is unchanged by this: the coordinator's answer is identical for every input.

SCOPE, STATED SO A SEAT CAN DISAGREE WITH ME. RSH-008's round-1 architecture seat ruled that change ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix BECAUSE it 'stays inside platform/orchestration/actions, adds no schema column, no new reserved key on a shared action config, no wire-shape change'. This one does NOT stay inside actions -- it adds an exported method to a type three packages import -- so I am not claiming that precedent transfers. It has therefore ALSO gone to the architecture-review track as RFC_019, in the same commit, and this submission is not asking the gate to substitute for that. What I do claim is that it changes no wire shape, no schema, no config vocabulary, and no guarantee any automated consumer relies on.

PROOF IS BY MUTATION, BECAUSE A GREEN SUITE CANNOT BE PROOF HERE. Every pre-existing test in the actions package pins error_code, action and message and passes sqlmock.AnyArg() for agent_type -- that was the original defect, so a broken ladder is green on the whole suite. Six mutations were run and the failure IDENTITIES checked, not just the counts: drop rung 1 -> 3/3/2 failures across types, actions, orchestration (the ladder really is shared); drop rung 2 -> the four PRE-EXISTING actions tests fail (the no-op half is pinned, not assumed); drop the nil guard -> only the nil case; revert the actions door to its old one-rung read -> EXACTLY the 3 new tests fail and nothing else, which is the defect reproduced and simultaneously the proof the old suite could not see it; make the coordinator stop delegating -> only the new coordinator test fails. determineOwnerAgentType had NO test before this change, which is why the fifth mutation matters: a claim of the form 'one ladder, two consumers' is worth as much as its least-pinned consumer.

THE EDIT LIST BELOW IS COMPLETE, NOT A SAMPLE. Seven files, four production and three test, and there is no eighth. (This lane's round 2 was REJECTED by the guardian for exactly this -- a 34-file change described by an 8-edit array -- so the completeness is stated rather than assumed.) One further file changed in the same commit and is NOT code: the concept-register entry RSH-009, which the platform-seams ruling requires to ship in the same commit as the seam.

KNOWN LIMITATION, DECLARED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED BY A SEAT. This may be a partial no-op on RESUMED steps. RunAgentType reaches the actions door on the first-step / same-message path (processor sets it at messaging/processor.go:1828 -> ToHeaders -> FromHeaders -> buildActionParams hands the same execCtx to the action). On a step resumed after an await, execCtx is rebuilt from the RESPONSE message's headers, and ensureFullExecutionContext (coordinator.go:1589) backfills Sender from state.OwnerAgentType ONLY when Sender is empty -- it does not backfill RunAgentType at all. I could not settle this by measurement because orchestration_states retains ~24h and every actions-door generic row is older than that, so the decisive check is post-roll and is written into the register entry's verify-later. The contained remedy, if the residue does not fall, is one if in ensureFullExecutionContext backfilling RunAgentType from state.OwnerAgentType; it is deliberately NOT taken here because it adds a rung sourced from durable state and belongs in its own round.

plan.summary: Hoist the two CONTEXT rungs of the 'which agent is running' ladder onto types.ExecutionContext as ResolvedAgentType(), and have both consumers -- coordinator.determineOwnerAgentType and actions.runningStepProvenance -- climb it instead of each keeping its own. The pod-env rung and the 'generic' filler stay coordinator-side on purpose. Behaviour change: an agent_error_log row filed under the running step is credited to the resolved real agent instead of the dispatch-path sender. No schema, no wire shape, no config vocabulary.

edits.rationale: types is the only package BOTH consumers import (go list: 1 each), and both rungs are fields of this struct, so this is the hoist target the compiler allows -- actions cannot import orchestration, the cycle is real. The method stops at the context and returns "" rather than taking a fallback parameter: the two consumers' tails genuinely differ, and a parameter would make them look identical while behaving differently. Nil-receiver safe so a call site does not need a nil check to ask the question.

Delegates its two context rungs and keeps its own two. The answer is identical for every input -- this consumer's behaviour does not change -- which is the point: the drift is closed by making the OTHER consumer agree with this one, not by moving this one.

The defect site. It reads the shared ladder instead of Sender.AgentType alone, and KEEPS params.AgentType as its own floor below the context -- that floor is state.OwnerAgentType, this ladder's durable output, and is the right answer here and the wrong one in the coordinator. step_name resolution is untouched. Every one of the six RSH-008 doors reaches production through this one function, so this is the whole of the write-path change.

Comment only, no behaviour. It warned that provenance here resolves to 'generic' and that the hoist was out of scope; both statements are now false, and it also carried the stale 25-row sample. Corrected VISIBLY in place rather than deleted, per this estate's correction discipline -- a silently-fixed comment loses the record that the sizing was wrong.

Pins the ladder where it now lives. Each case names the rung it kills, so a failure reads as a diagnosis rather than a diff. The environment test is the one that stops the next author 'completing' the ladder by adding the coordinator's third rung. The round-trip test pins the WIRE, not the ladder: run_agent_type has to be in BOTH ToHeaders and FromHeaders or the resolved type dies at the topic boundary and every consumer silently falls back to the sender.

determineOwnerAgentType had NO test at all -- this is the first. Without it the delegation is unpinned on one side, and the drift this change closes could simply come back through the coordinator with every test still green (mutation M5 confirms: reverting the delegation fails ONLY this test). It also pins that the pod-env rung and the 'generic' filler stayed HERE, which is the design decision the rationale rests on.

The four that fail against the pre-hoist door and pass after. Three drive the new rung (the simple door, the findings door -- which resolves identity once and then REWRITES every Context, exactly where a shared fix has been lost before -- and the demoted diagnostic on an unattributed row, which would otherwise name the wrong agent and misdirect a human). The fourth drives params.AgentType, the floor NOTHING drove before even though the fixture always carried it. jsonValueIs is new because jsonHas would pass on a diagnostic naming the WRONG agent, and a misdirecting diagnostic is worse than an absent one. The existing fixture deliberately leaves RunAgentType empty, so all pre-existing tests pass unchanged -- that is the no-op half of the proof and is the half normally skipped.
edits.sketch:
func resolvedRunParams(db *sql.DB) ActionParams {
	params := runningStepParams(db)
	params.ExecutionContext.RunAgentType = "resolved-real-agent"
	params.ExecutionContext.Sender.AgentType = "generic"   // the live shape
	return params
}
// then: expect arg 5 == "resolved-real-agent", NOT "generic"
mock.ExpectExec(regexp.QuoteMeta(insertRE)).WithArgs(
	"site-1", "example.com", "item-1234", "orch-1234",
	"resolved-real-agent", "agent-id-1", "pod-1", "running_step",
	"an_action", "boom", "A_CODE", "error",
	jsonLacks{"provenance_missing"})

grounded_in: types/context.go:62 -- 'RunAgentType is the RESOLVED real agent type whose workflow is executing (from config.agent_type / the loaded agent definition), as opposed to the dispatch-path sender which is often generic. Set by the processor before executing a workflow; consumed by the coordinator's determineOwnerAgentType so owner_agent_type records the real agent, not generic (bugs_open/060).' -- the field documents a single consumer, and that was literally true until this change.

actions/log_action_error.go:118 (pre-change) -- 'agentType, stepName = params.AgentType, params.CurrentStep; if params.ExecutionContext.Sender.AgentType != "" { agentType = params.ExecutionContext.Sender.AgentType }' -- the second rung only.

coordinator.go:1691 -- buildActionParams sets 'AgentType: state.OwnerAgentType', so the actions door's floor IS the coordinator ladder's own durable output. This is the measurement behind refusing to move the pod-env rung: params.AgentType is strictly more specific than os.Getenv(AGENT_TYPE) here.

coordinator.go:1589 -- ensureFullExecutionContext fills Sender from state.OwnerAgentType ONLY 'if execCtx.Sender.AgentType == ""', and never fills RunAgentType. This is the evidence for the declared resumed-step limitation, and it is why that limitation is stated rather than claimed away.

go list -f '{{range .Imports}}{{println .}}{{end}}' ./platform/orchestration | grep -x .../orchestration/actions -> FOUND (the cycle is real, delegation coordinator-ward is impossible); the same command for ./platform/orchestration/actions and ./platform/orchestration against .../orchestration/types -> 1 and 1 (types is a valid hoist target for both).

Live 2026-08-08, agent_error_log: 'SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE occurred_at < 2026-07-27) AS before, count(*) FILTER (WHERE occurred_at >= 2026-07-27) AS after FROM agent_error_log WHERE agent_type = generic' -> 499 / 56. baf887a8e (RunAgentType, 2026-07-26) is the boundary, and the dominant producer call_agent/call_dispatch (394 rows) has max(occurred_at) 2026-07-25. This is the measurement that falsifies the 559-row framing the work was commissioned on.

Live 2026-08-08: 'SELECT agent_type, step_name, action, count(*), max(occurred_at) FROM agent_error_log WHERE error_code = REVIEW_SUPERSEDED_BY_PASSING_SAVE GROUP BY 1,2,3' -> generic | (null) | reconcile_superseded_reviews | 25 | 2026-07-23 11:22:30Z. All 25 on one day, a month old.

Live 2026-08-08: the three actions-door producers of a generic row since 2026-07-27 are diagnose_council_decide (31, via LogActionFindings at diagnose_council_decide_action.go:643), retract_page_deployment (4, via LogActionError at retract_page_deployment_action.go:419/456) and emit_tool_cross_link_items (1, create_tool_cross_link_items.go:398) = 36 rows in 13 days. The other 20 are orchestrate/process_message/coordinator paths this change does not touch.

Live 2026-08-08: 'SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = agent_error_log' includes idx_error_log_agent ON (agent_type, occurred_at DESC) -- the column this change corrects is the entry point of the table's investigation index.

Mutation harness, run 2026-08-08 across all three packages: baseline 0/0/0 failures; drop rung 1 -> 3/3/2; drop rung 2 -> 3 (types) and the 4 PRE-EXISTING actions tests; drop nil guard -> 1 (types only, and 0 elsewhere, because both consumers nil-check before calling -- the guard is defence for future callers, stated rather than overclaimed); revert the actions door to Sender.AgentType -> exactly the 3 new tests and nothing else; revert the coordinator delegation -> exactly the new coordinator test.
plan.risks:
SCOPE. This adds an exported method to types.ExecutionContext, which platform/orchestration, platform/orchestration/actions and platform/messaging all import. RSH-008's round-1 architecture seat ruled that change point_fix BECAUSE it stayed inside actions; this one does not, so I am NOT claiming the precedent transfers, and it has gone to the architecture track as RFC_019 in the same commit. If the seat still reads it as architecture-scope, that is a useful signal and not a contradiction of this submission.

SEMANTIC CHANGE TO A POPULATED COLUMN. agent_error_log.agent_type means something slightly different after this for rows filed under declared inheritance: the resolved run agent rather than the dispatch sender. Censused rather than asserted -- no automated consumer branches on its value (3 Go readers, 0 live config steps, 1 repo SQL script, all listed in the rationale); the consumers are humans and the diagnosis bundle. The 499 historical generic rows do NOT change: this is write-path only.

PARTIAL NO-OP ON RESUMED STEPS, declared above rather than left to be discovered. RunAgentType is not backfilled by ensureFullExecutionContext, so a step resumed from a response whose headers lacked run_agent_type will still fall through to the sender. Undecidable before the roll because orchestration_states retains ~24h; the post-roll check and its 36-row baseline are written into RSH-009's verify-later, and a zero there is only meaningful alongside the total-rows positive control.

ROLLBACK is image-only: no schema, no config, no migration. The previous binary tolerates every row this one writes.

The actions package currently has ONE unrelated failing test at committed HEAD (TestValidDocSubjectTypes_LockstepWithMigrationCheck, another lane adding a 'decision' doc subject_type). Verified pre-existing by running it against a clean 'git archive HEAD' tree. It is named here so a seat does not read it as this change's, and it is deliberately NOT fixed here -- that would be another lane's work riding in this commit.
